scope: Corollary 2.6 (Restarted support in open sets) of the manuscript “An explicit exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE” (preprints/An-explicit-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-26-2026/An-explicit-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-26-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 230 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c6e7116ea33f29ee), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: At a finite stopping time τ for ordinary chordal SLE in H, fix a realized past for which the conditional continuation law Pτ is defined. Let D be its surviving domain, and let F : H → D send 0 to the current tip prime end and infinity to the target. Use its continuous spherical extension on H. Let α : [0, 1] → H be a continuous simple path with α(0) = 0 and α((0, 1]) ⊂ H. If O is relatively open in D and contains F(α[0, 1]), and V ⊂ D is an open neighborhood of F(α(1)), then the restarted half-plane trace e γ satisfies Pτ {for some t < ∞, F(e γ[0, t]) ⊂ O and F(e γ(t)) ∈ V } > 0. The same statement holds for a Euclidean similarity of the evolution. The positive probability may depend on the realized past, α, O, and V .
